pull_request.title: Tracker: benchmark GBTS reconstruction with Fatras and Geant4
pull_request.head: codex/tracker-gbts-reconstruction
pull_request.body:
Adds a full measured-hit tracker reconstruction benchmark on the current balanced Gen-3 geometry: Gaussian digitization → pixel space points → native ACTS GBTS → hit-estimated parameters → all-system CKF → ambiguity resolution, at constant 3 T and |η|≤4.

The selected GBTS profile was frozen after 13 paired muon tuning profiles. The extension adds Fatras electrons and Geant4 muons, electrons and charged pions at pT 1/5/10/100 GeV, with **5,000 generated events per new point (80,000 total)**. The original Fatras muon reference is preserved. No species validation result was used for seeder retuning.

| Population | 1 GeV | 5 GeV | 10 GeV | 100 GeV |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Fatras single muons | 97.18% | 99.28% | 99.30% | 99.44% |
| Fatras single electrons | 51.72% | 83.70% | 86.18% | 86.10% |
| Geant4 single muons | 96.10% | 98.78% | 99.06% | 98.76% |
| Geant4 single electrons | 53.04% | 78.84% | 81.76% | 78.68% |
| Geant4 single pions | 80.66% | 86.48% | 87.02% | 89.58% |

Each efficiency uses its own generated-event denominator. Full signed-η/pT resolutions, six-parameter integrated pulls, uncut tails, wrong charge, secondary matches, unmatched candidates and duplicates are retained with uncertainty intervals. Populations are not pooled.

Electron momentum/charge reconstruction needs further work: Fatras electrons at 100 GeV have 520/4,305 wrong charges and 2,285 pT errors beyond 50%; their central relative-pT width is 102.93%. Geant4 electrons at 100 GeV have 523/3,934 wrong charges, 2,099 pT errors beyond 50% and a central width of 82.04%. Geant4 pions at 100 GeV retain 141/4,479 wrong charges and substantial momentum/pull tails. Narrow electron pull cores do not establish calibrated uncertainties.

Electrons use native one-way multicomponent bremsstrahlung CKF; muons/pions retain ordinary two-way CKF. One configured species hypothesis is applied uniformly to every seed in each sample, without per-track truth PID. Gaussian response is species independent and unmerged. Geant4 transports detailed DD4hep material while Fatras/CKF use the retained effective ACTS map; this is not a pure transport-model comparison or a new material map. The 25 ns Geant4 limit remains explicit, with time-kill incidence reported. Single-particle results do not establish pileup performance.

Validation includes all 16 completed native cases, exact 46,250-sensor Geant4 mapping and event counts, frozen input/source/runtime identities, complete ROOT event/measurement/candidate and fitted-tuple audits, and independent classification of all new events. ACTS FPE checks remain unmasked; Geant4-internal BeamOn monitoring has its documented native limitation. Task-owned SafeFatras avoids rounded-away libm underflows without changing sampling/physics; all 15,000 original/passing 1/5/10 GeV native audit streams and all nine ROOT tree contents agree bitwise. Failed/interrupted attempts remain diagnostic evidence.

Human reviewer `asalzburger-review` approved revision `78d22297e2518ef674ebf1601215fd17c6b93b71` on 2026-10-30 as the current tracker reconstruction baseline ([public approval](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/107#pullrequestreview-5713182516)). The user confirms approval of the PR, tuning and cross-checks. DES041 remains DRAFT / isolated PROTOTYPE under the separate formal detector-design lifecycle. Geometry, field, material prescription, frozen response and scientific benchmark data are unchanged.

Final accounting records **131,656,491 observed tokens across 26 completed turns / 744 requests**: 131,180,836 input and 475,655 output. Cached input 128,479,872 and reasoning output 194,352 are subsets. The active coordinator turn remains excluded, so this is a partial subtotal; actual models/client version remain unknown. Exact counters have one canonical owner per turn. Public approval and 26 allowlisted completed-turn discussion snapshots are retained, with private state and tool arguments/results excluded. [Approval and accounting record](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/codex/tracker-gbts-reconstruction/docs/validation/tracker-reconstruction-approval.md).

[Species results and full plots](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/157994cbcbc2ec3551dc6bcbad51b3fc9c0a212e/docs/validation/tracker-reconstruction-species/results.md) · [Original muon tuning/validation](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/157994cbcbc2ec3551dc6bcbad51b3fc9c0a212e/docs/validation/tracker-reconstruction/results.md) · [Execution guide](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/157994cbcbc2ec3551dc6bcbad51b3fc9c0a212e/software/analysis/tracker_reconstruction/README.md)

Adds a full measured-hit tracker reconstruction benchmark on the current balanced Gen-3 geometry: Gaussian digitization → pixel space points → native ACTS GBTS → hit-estimated parameters → all-system CKF → ambiguity resolution, at constant 3 T and |η|≤4.

The selected GBTS profile was frozen after 13 paired muon tuning profiles. The extension adds Fatras electrons and Geant4 muons, electrons and charged pions at pT 1/5/10/100 GeV, with **5,000 generated events per new point (80,000 total)**. The original Fatras muon reference is preserved. No species validation result was used for seeder retuning.

| Population | 1 GeV | 5 GeV | 10 GeV | 100 GeV |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Fatras single muons | 97.18% | 99.28% | 99.30% | 99.44% |
| Fatras single electrons | 51.72% | 83.70% | 86.18% | 86.10% |
| Geant4 single muons | 96.10% | 98.78% | 99.06% | 98.76% |
| Geant4 single electrons | 53.04% | 78.84% | 81.76% | 78.68% |
| Geant4 single pions | 80.66% | 86.48% | 87.02% | 89.58% |

Each efficiency uses its own generated-event denominator. Full signed-η/pT resolutions, six-parameter integrated pulls, uncut tails, wrong charge, secondary matches, unmatched candidates and duplicates are retained with uncertainty intervals. Populations are not pooled.

Electron momentum/charge reconstruction needs further work: Fatras electrons at 100 GeV have 520/4,305 wrong charges and 2,285 pT errors beyond 50%; their central relative-pT width is 102.93%. Geant4 electrons at 100 GeV have 523/3,934 wrong charges, 2,099 pT errors beyond 50% and a central width of 82.04%. Geant4 pions at 100 GeV retain 141/4,479 wrong charges and substantial momentum/pull tails. Narrow electron pull cores do not establish calibrated uncertainties.

Electrons use native one-way multicomponent bremsstrahlung CKF; muons/pions retain ordinary two-way CKF. One configured species hypothesis is applied uniformly to every seed in each sample, without per-track truth PID. Gaussian response is species independent and unmerged. Geant4 transports detailed DD4hep material while Fatras/CKF use the retained effective ACTS map; this is not a pure transport-model comparison or a new material map. The 25 ns Geant4 limit remains explicit, with time-kill incidence reported. Single-particle results do not establish pileup performance.

Validation includes all 16 completed native cases, exact 46,250-sensor Geant4 mapping and event counts, frozen input/source/runtime identities, complete ROOT event/measurement/candidate and fitted-tuple audits, and independent classification of all new events. ACTS FPE checks remain unmasked; Geant4-internal BeamOn monitoring has its documented native limitation. Task-owned SafeFatras avoids rounded-away libm underflows without changing sampling/physics; all 15,000 original/passing 1/5/10 GeV native audit streams and all nine ROOT tree contents agree bitwise. Failed/interrupted attempts remain diagnostic evidence.

Human reviewer `asalzburger-review` approved revision `78d22297e2518ef674ebf1601215fd17c6b93b71` on 2026-10-30 as the current tracker reconstruction baseline ([public approval](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/107#pullrequestreview-5713182516)). Geometry, field, material prescription, frozen response and scientific benchmark data are unchanged.

Cached input 128,479,872 and reasoning output 194,352 are subsets. The active coordinator turn remains excluded, so this is a partial subtotal; actual models/client version remain unknown. Exact counters have one canonical owner per turn. Public approval and 26 allowlisted completed-turn discussion snapshots are retained, with private state and tool arguments/results excluded. [Approval and accounting record](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/codex/tracker-gbts-reconstruction/docs/validation/tracker-reconstruction-approval.md).

**RECO-PhysVal-01 completed.** Reviewed nODD **`616fd2aee1717adeead136a040bb07f1f58a2b99`** and clean ACTS source **`355ea68493b326956756c9386d2fd9eaf9328568`**. Read-only assessment; no files changed or native jobs run.

The proposed benchmark is appropriate: one origin muon/event, randomized charge, uniform signed η∈[−4,4] and full φ, pT=1/5/10/100 GeV, constant 3 T, frozen PR104 geometry/material and PR101 pooled Gaussian response.

**Findings to address before claiming reconstruction performance**

| Severity | Finding and evidence | Required handling |
|---|---|---|
| High | GBTS defaults to **2 T** in `GraphBasedSeedingAlgorithm.hpp:61–62`; Python `reconstruction.py:1453–1488` forwards only minPt. | Explicitly configure GBTS at **3 T**, separately from parameter estimation/CKF field configuration. |
| High | `TrackTruthMatcher.cpp:70–91` skips tracks lacking associations or whose majority particle is outside inputParticles. The collector excludes these from fake histogram filling (`PatternRecognitionPerformanceCollector.cpp:103–120`). | Audit every accepted track. Count missing classifications explicitly; never silently drop them from fake/contamination denominators. |
| High | Standard CKF helper matches `particles_selected` (`reconstruction.py:1977–1984`), while ambiguity helper matches `particles` (`:2370–2377`); Fatras aliases `particles` to simulated particles (`simulation.py:538`). | Schedule explicit stage matchers and truth inputs. Preserve generated-primary denominators, and separate real-secondary contamination from genuine unmatched candidates. |
| High | Native efficiency plots default to η∈[−3,3], omit the 5 GeV slice, and place 100 GeV at the upper pT edge (`EffPlotTool.hpp:40–59`). | Produce independent full-acceptance counters and four dedicated pT panels; account for under/overflow explicitly. |
| Medium | Native duplicate representative uses “more measurements **OR** lower χ²” (`TrackTruthMatcher.cpp:115–128`), which is order dependent. | Preserve native classifications for comparison; independently choose one deterministic best candidate for residuals and primary-efficiency accounting. |
| Medium | Standard GBTS helper requires `"clusters"` (`reconstruction.py:1485`), although Gaussian smearing produces no geometric clusters. | Adapter must support no-cluster input and keep cluster-width cuts disabled. |
| Medium | GBTS has experiment-specific volume vetoes and layer conventions (`GraphBasedSeedingAlgorithm.cpp:310–313, 412–419`). | Verify all 24 pixel logical groups, including added ID10, through physical sensor identities and actual positions rather than importing ITk numbering rules. |

**Recommended fixed definitions**

Freeze these before tuning; the numerical cuts below are study choices, not human acceptance requirements.

- **Generated efficiency:** generated primaries with ≥1 accepted qualifying primary-matched candidate / **all generated primaries**. Include no-hit, no-seed, fit-failure and acceptance-hole events.
- **Conditional efficiency:** the same efficiency restricted to primaries with **≥6 unique sensitive-sensor measurements and ≥3 distinct physical pixel logical groups**. Also show a nested ≥4-pixel-group denominator: default `minSeedLevel=3` requires a triplet plus confirmation (`GraphBasedTrackSeeder.hpp:153–155`). Do not replace the headline denominator with that easier subset.
- **Matching:** unique shared inlier measurement indices; exclude outliers. Set explicit **purity≥0.5 and completeness≥0.5**, consistent with native doubleMatching. Completeness denominator is every unique measurement associated with that particle before reconstruction; deduplicate measurement–particle pairs first. Native contribution counting is in `TrackClassification.cpp:96–124`.
- **Duplicates:** additional qualifying candidates beyond one best candidate/particle. Deterministic representative: maximum inlier measurement count, then minimum χ²/ndf, then stable track index. Report duplicate candidates/all accepted candidates and fraction of generated events with duplicates.
- **Fake fraction:** unmatched accepted candidates/all accepted candidates, with candidates matched to real simulated secondaries reported separately. If only generated-primary truth is available, title the combined quantity **“unmatched-to-primary fraction”**.
- **Wrong charge:** wrong-sign q/p among primary-matched representatives. Report separately: a track can use the right measurements and still have a catastrophically wrong fit.
- **Seed efficiency:** primary has ≥1 seed whose distinct source measurements all belong to it, with ≥3 distinct pixel groups; report before parameter estimation and after successful estimation. Also retain loose-majority seed matching as a diagnostic.
- **Stage counts:** generated → truth-associated measurements → pixel SPs → raw GBTS seeds → estimated seeds → CKF candidates → accepted tracks → ambiguity survivors. Retain no-output events at every stage.

All six perigee residual/pull distributions should use one deterministic primary representative, consistent `(truth−reconstructed)/σreco`, wrapped φ residuals, and full uncut tails. Time is prior-dominated without timed measurements; `TrackParamsEstimationAlgorithm.cpp:273` initializes untimed seeds at zero.

**Practical bounded campaign**

1. Smoke: 100 events/pT; inspect stage accounting and source identities.
2. Connection training: **1,000 events/pT**, independent seeds; cover both η signs and all four pT values. Freeze and hash the resulting connection table.
3. Tuning: **500 events/pT**, shared generated/smeared events across configurations; maximum **12 candidate profiles plus one documented default control**.
4. Untouched validation: **5,000 events/pT**, one frozen configuration across all four momenta.

A practical initial 12-profile scan is minPt∈{0.4,0.6,0.8} GeV × nominal/looser coherent tau cuts × confirmed seeds/triplet fallback. Confirm available adapter controls first; make fallback acceptance reach |η|=4 instead of inheriting the native 1.5 limit. Hold CKF and ambiguity cuts fixed initially so changes can be attributed to GBTS. Record every attempted profile, including failures.

Choose from the tuning Pareto frontier. A defensible predeclared tie-break is: highest worst-pT generated efficiency, then highest equally weighted four-pT efficiency, then lower fake-event incidence, duplicates and runtime. Use paired event outcomes to identify statistically indistinguishable efficiency changes. Publish the Pareto table; no arbitrary numerical target should be presented as a user requirement. If validation results motivate retuning, acquire a new untouched validation sample.

**Uncertainties and interpretation**

Use Wilson intervals for primary efficiency and event-level duplicate/fake incidence. Tracks and seeds within an event are correlated: candidate-fraction Wilson intervals are approximate; prefer event-block bootstrap for nonzero candidate fake/duplicate fractions.

For **zero fake events**, give the exact one-sided 95% upper bound:

`1 − 0.05^(1/N_generated_events)`.

At 5,000 events/pT this is **0.0599%**. In signed η bins of width0.5, approximately312 events/bin gives a bound near **0.96%**. Do not claim “fake-free.” Single-muon data do not test combinatorial fakes under pile-up or dense occupancy.

**Required anti-bias/native audit**

- GBTS/SP/parameter-estimation/CKF declared inputs must contain no truth track grouping, truth momenta, truth hit filtering or truth-derived seed parameters.
- Pixel SP coordinates must reproduce native measured-local→global conversion. The proper implementation is `SpacePointMaker.cpp:44–73`; truth positions/times are legitimate for independent **connection training only**.
- CKF must see the complete unfiltered pixel/short-strip/long-strip measurement collection; particle-selection helpers may define evaluation sets only.
- Record all source links and source measurement indices for raw/estimated seeds and final tracks, plus stage failures, per-system inliers/holes/outliers, covariance validity and reference-surface presence.
- Verify frozen measurement variances and dimensions: systems1–5 two-dimensional;6–7 one-dimensional. Preserve existing bounded-Gaussian retry behavior.
- Join geometry/calibration/material by physical sensor/layer semantics: PR104 documents **602 permuted ACTS IDs** in added logicalID10. Copying old per-sensor numeric-ID payloads is not justified.
- Fingerprint actual executable libraries, adapter/configuration, geometry/map/error inputs and outputs before/after execution; source HEAD alone does not prove runtime identity.

Actual checks: read the pinned five nODD inputs, repository/role instructions, exact clean ACTS matching/GBTS/SP/parameter/helper/writer sources, and inspected existing truth-tracking observer code. Spack source preflight returned **unverified** because setup/lock fingerprints changed and full DD4hep/Geant4 sources remain unverified; this assessment did not depend on their runtime. Final native implementation/results require a separate pinned independent review.

The coordinator has agreed to remove this internal selector and retain completed CKF output before independent quality selection. Propagation/smoothing errors still require separate diagnostics; absence of an output is not an exact fit-error count.

2. **Time units — medium.** Analyzer:157–164 preserves ACTS time in **ct[mm]**, not ns. ACTS `Units.hpp:120–126` defines1ns=299.792458 native units. Convert time residuals and covariance for ns plots, or label ct[mm] explicitly. Pulls remain unchanged. The smoke mean386.225 corresponds to1.288ns.

Store ordered space-point indices and source links in addition to the unique measurement set. Also guard state `referenceSurface()` access at:50. The coordinator is implementing both corrections.

Use event-stage timing, or separately recorded reconstruction execution time, for the runtime selection tie-break.

Runtime hashes are start-only; add launch/close checks for runtime, effective inputs and loaded DD4hep factory libraries before final validation.

**SPECIES-SoftEng-05: read-only assessment complete**, against `17a4b2e8831081ddfdfb625c3eee15c52862befa`. No files, processes or runtime settings changed.

ACTS/Fatras range execution is technically supported. **Geant4 cannot currently preserve identical internal event numbering**, and its fresh-run equivalence remains unproven. I recommend leaving both active jobs unchanged.

- ACTS `Sequencer(skip=S, events=M)` processes absolute event contexts **[S,S+M)**; `events` is a count. See matching ACTS355ea `Examples/Framework/src/Framework/Sequencer.cpp:223–282,470–525`.
- RNG seeds hash **configured seed, absolute event number and numeric algorithm slot**. Names themselves are not hashed. Decorator count and complete sequence ordering must remain identical. See `RandomNumbers.cpp:23–25`.
- Generation, Gaussian smearing and GBTS use event-local RNG/storage; reviewed counters appear observational. Fresh-process Fatras equivalence is therefore plausible, but still requires exact replay tests.
- Geant4 reseeds from that ACTS context and resets its event store before each event: `Examples/Algorithms/Geant4/src/Geant4Simulation.cpp:126–147`.
- However, `SimParticleTranslation.cpp:42` overwrites `G4Event` IDs using a private counter starting at zero. The persistent helper separately calls `ProcessOneEvent(processed)` with another local zero-based counter: project `TruthTracking.cpp:119–143`. **ACTS skip advances neither counter.**
- Fresh batches also repeat `RunInitialization/InitializeEventLoop` after the first event’s seed is set. Whether this or other Geant4 run-level state changes transport needs experimental proof; reviewed ACTS actions do not establish that internal IDs and initialization are irrelevant.

A future standalone launcher could leave frozen files intact and supply a narrow ACTS proxy to the existing `run()` function that changes only Sequencer construction to `skip=S, events=M`. It must add no sequence element, preserve all decorators/slots, use one thread per process, retain the original seed/configuration and fingerprint itself. For Geant4, `persistent_handle(M)` must retain **M local events**, not `S+M`.

Required proof before adopting batches:

1. Compare monolithic versus fresh-process split ranges using identical binaries, including nonzero/high offsets and **the first event of each fresh range**.
2. Require exact per-event JSON rows: generated/simulated particles, measurements, space points, ordered seeds, CKF/ambiguity outputs and states. ROOT branch values must agree exactly at persisted precision.
3. Verify scientific input payloads, geometry mappings, algorithm/decorator order, source/runtime identities and unchanged FPE gates across processes.
4. Treat any Geant4 discrepancy as a blocker. Literal equality of internal G4 event IDs already fails with the existing helper.

Aggregation also requires a new explicit contract. The current runner exposes no skip and existing `species_evidence.py:91,111` requires one completed 5,000-event report. A batch aggregate must instead retain every completed child report, prove each requested range and native count, and require the disjoint union to equal **exactly events 0…4999**. It must never represent summed child counts as one native process.

Keep each batch’s ROOT files and hashes; audit them separately. Sort event rows globally and recompute metrics, quantiles and bootstrap intervals over the resulting 5,000 events. Do not average shard summaries or count repeated proof events twice. ROOT/gzip/report container bytes will differ because of metadata and compression; byte equality should concern canonical event rows and persisted numerical payloads.
